root_cause.text: The bounds check for 128-byte SQE operations in io_init_req() used the logical SQ head position (ctx->cached_sq_head) instead of the physical SQE index, allowing an attacker to remap a 128-byte operation to the last physical slot via sq_array, resulting in an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` with `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1`. The commit message explains that the old check is correct only for NO_SQARRAY rings (where physical == logical) and that when sq_array is present, setting `sq_array[N] = sq_entries - 1` places a 128-byte operation at the last physical SQE slot, causing a 64-byte read past the end of the array in `io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy()`.

intent_record.how: The new condition checks if the current SQE index is at or beyond the last valid entry in the SQ ring, returning -EINVAL when a two-entry operation would wrap around the ring buffer. Previously, the condition incorrectly used the head pointer's alignment to the ring size.
